title: Annals of St Vincent, Metz: Hungarians defeated by Otto, 955
fact_summary: An annal from Metz for 955 records that the Hungarians, who had entered Lothar's kingdom for the fourth time, were defeated by Otto, whom it calls emperor.

place.label: The annal names no battle site

claims.text: The entry for 955 reads: “Ungarii, qui iam quarto regnum Lotharii intraverant, ab Ottone imperatore devincuntur”, in Laura Gazzoli's translation “The Hungarians, who had now entered the kingdom of Lothar for the fourth time, were defeated by the Emperor Otto.”
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: The continuation of Regino's chronicle places the same defeat “apud Lichum fluvium”, at the river Lech.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

dating_methods.text: Dated by the year heading of the annal (s.a. 955). The entry gives no day or place.
dating_methods.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in the open copy linked under Sources.

open_questions.text: When, and by whom, was this entry written?
The Metz annal names no place. Two other sources name the river Lech; where on the river was it?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.

change_notes.note: An earlier open question asked where the battle was. Regino's continuator has now been read, and names the river Lech (claim c2).
